specification: Implement a small dependency resolver and lock-file generator in the `resolver` package, spread over four files. `resolver/versions.py` defines `parse_version`, `format_version` and `newest`; `resolver/solver.py` defines exceptions `ResolutionError` and `ConflictError` (a subclass of ResolutionError) and `resolve(registry, requirements)`; `resolver/lockfile.py` defines `render_lock(registry, resolution)`, `parse_lock(text)` and `generate_lock(registry, requirements)`; `resolver/__init__.py` re-exports all of these names. A version is a string `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` of exactly three non-negative decimal integers written with ASCII digits only and without leading zeros (except the single digit 0). `parse_version(text)` returns the tuple of three ints; it raises TypeError if text is not a str and ValueError if it is malformed (no whitespace, no suffixes). `format_version(parts)` joins a sequence of exactly three ints with dots and raises ValueError for any other length. `newest(versions, major)` takes an iterable of version strings (a dict of versions is iterated by key), validates every one of them with `parse_version` (so a malformed entry raises ValueError even if its major differs), and returns the numerically highest version whose major equals `major` as a string, or None if there is none. A registry maps package name to a dict that maps version string to the dependencies of that version, itself a dict mapping package name to the required major version (a non-negative int that is not a bool; otherwise TypeError for a wrong type and ValueError for a negative value). `requirements` is a dict of the same shape for the root. `resolve(registry, requirements)` chooses for every package that is needed, directly or transitively, the newest version having the required major, and returns a dict mapping package name to chosen version string, ordered by package name. Only the dependencies of the chosen version of a package are followed. Requirements are processed first-in first-out, starting with the root requirements in name order and then, for each newly chosen package, its dependencies in name order. Root requirements are all validated before anything is resolved. When a package is needed again, the same major is fine and a different major raises ConflictError. A package missing from the registry, or one with no version of the required major, raises ResolutionError (not ConflictError). Dependency cycles are legal. An empty requirements dict gives an empty dict. The canonical lock text, which render_lock and generate_lock return, starts with the line `# lock v1`, followed by one line per resolved package in name order: `name==version`, with ` requires dep@major,dep@major` appended (dependencies in name order, no spaces after commas) if the chosen version has dependencies; the text ends with a newline. `render_lock(registry, resolution)` takes a resolution dict (in any order) and renders it, looking dependencies up in the registry (a missing entry raises KeyError). `parse_lock(text)` returns a dict mapping name to `(version, dependencies_dict)`. It accepts more than the canonical text: package lines may come in any order, the dependencies on a line may come in any order, and the final newline is optional, so the header alone, with or without a trailing newline, is a valid text. The first line must be exactly the header; later lines that are empty or start with `#` are ignored; every other line must match the package line format above exactly (package names are lowercase letters, digits and hyphens starting with a letter; the version must be valid; majors are decimal ints without leading zeros; no spaces other than the single ones of ` requires `). The only line end is the character `\n`: a carriage return anywhere in the text, comment lines included, makes the text malformed. A duplicate package or a duplicate dependency within a line is an error. Malformed text raises ValueError, a non-str argument TypeError. `generate_lock(registry, requirements)` resolves and renders in one step.
